properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. It argues for nothing and settles nothing. Prompted by Anthony bringing arXiv 2504.19874v1 (TurboQuant) on 2026-09-10 and asking whether anything in it was useful; the sizing and timing behind it are `fact:quantised-vectors-would-fit-in-the-export-and-full-precision-ones-would-not`, recorded against the parent decision so a reader of that node finds the evidence there.

WHY THIS IS NOT POINT 8 ON `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption`, since that node absorbs updates as numbered points and the duplicate guard offered exactly that route. The parent's NAME is the thing being questioned — "should reflow2 adopt embeddings AND THE HNSW INDEX" — and a question about a node's framing cannot be asked from inside it without rewriting the name that `what_next` and the orientation read back. The two also answer separately: the parent asks whether to adopt at all, this asks whether the option it has been arguing about is the right one, and settling either leaves the other open.

THE OBSERVATION. The parent has bundled two things since 2026-08-01. Its case-against has four legs — model dependency, thin-install, determinism, per-project state — and NOTICE WHICH LEG THE INDEX CARRIES: *"determinism is load-bearing: two runs of a detector must agree, and AN ANN INDEX IS APPROXIMATE BY CONSTRUCTION."* That objection is about HNSW. It is not about vectors.

MEASURED 2026-09-10, exhaustive cosine over 768-dim float32, unoptimised numpy on this box:
  4,102 nodes (this design today)     1.61 ms/query
  20,000 nodes                        6.18 ms/query
  100,000 nodes                      35.92 ms/query
A Rust SIMD scan over 2-bit quantised vectors would be faster again. So across reflow2's whole realistic size range — including the brownfield end, a decade-old instrument stack — AN APPROXIMATE INDEX BUYS NOTHING. HNSW exists to avoid a linear scan that costs milliseconds here.

THE OPTIONS, none preferred:

(a) LEAVE THE QUESTION AS POSED. Embeddings and HNSW together, decided together. Cheapest — no second node to keep current — and correct if the model leg is what actually binds, in which case the index half is never reached.

(b) RE-POSE IT AS "EMBEDDINGS, NO ANN INDEX". Quantised vectors, exact exhaustive scan, vectors carried in the export at ~7% of its size at 2 bits. This REMOVES the determinism leg rather than answering it: an exhaustive scan over fixed vectors returns the same ranking every time, so a detector fed by it can still agree with itself and `req:deterministic-core` is untouched. CONDITION, not a footnote: TurboQuant's random rotation must be SEEDED AND FROZEN in the record, or the vectors are not reproducible across machines and the byte-stable export is lost — an unseeded rotation would put a determinism hole in the one place this option claims to close one.

(c) AS (b) BUT ON THE INGEST-RESOLUTION PATH ONLY, where point 5 of the parent already located the weaker objection: that path's output is a merge_candidate a human rules on, not a verdict. Narrowest, and it is the path where point 4 says the lexical answer is genuinely blind — "Read Cache" ~ "Local Store" is not a low token_sort_ratio, it is invisible.

(d) NOTHING CHANGES. The model dependency was always the binding constraint, so re-framing the index half moves no decision. **This may simply be right, and it is the option to beat.**

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it:

⚠️ THE STRONGEST LEG IS UNTOUCHED. Quantization compresses vectors somebody else produced. It says nothing about whether reflow2 may depend on an embedding model, and `req:thin-install` and the one-binary posture stand exactly as they did. Option (d) rests on this and is not a straw man.

⚠️ OVER-ENGINEERING, AND THE SHAPE OF IT IS THE FAMILIAR ONE. 4,102 nodes is small. A vector path justified by reflow2's OWN graph would be a solution looking for a problem. If this earns its keep at all it is on CONSUMER graphs — a heterogeneous corpus where forty authors name one component forty ways — never on this one, and `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` is the test. Any argument from reflow2's own retrieval should be read as the tell rather than as the case.

⚠️ IT WOULD MAKE THE EXPORT DIFF NOISIER. ~1 MB of base64 that churns whenever text changes, inside a document CI diffs and `dec:export-hash-chain` chains. The carriage benefit and the reviewable-diff cost pull against each other and nothing here weighs them.

⚠️ AND IT IS NOT THE ANSWER TO THE RETRIEVAL FAILURE THIS WEEK. `fact:a-settled-question-was-re-asked-because-the-requirements-prose-outlived-its-decision` was a search miss whose cause was structural: the Decision that GOVERNS a node is about a different subject than any query about that node, so semantic similarity would likely have missed it too. The relation was already an edge; the fix was reading the edge. Citing that incident in favour of embeddings would be reading the wrong lesson from real evidence, and it is the misreading most available to the next session that finds this node.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether a consumer has actually been hurt by lexical convergence on a heterogeneous corpus. That is a field question, not a benchmark — and until one has been, (d) holds.
properties.name: OPEN — has the embeddings question been posed against the wrong option? At this scale an exact exhaustive scan beats an ANN index, and HNSW is what carries the determinism objection
properties.rationale: The parent decision bundles "embeddings" with "HNSW", and its determinism objection attaches specifically to the approximate index rather than to the vectors. Measured at 1.61 ms/query on this design and 36 ms at 100k nodes, an ANN index buys nothing across reflow2's realistic range, so the bundled option may be the wrong one to have been arguing about for five weeks. Kept as a separate node because the parent's own NAME carries the framing under question and the two answer independently. Recorded as an idea rather than a proposal because the strongest leg of the case-against — the model dependency — is untouched by any of it, and because a vector path justified by reflow2's own 4,102-node graph would be exactly the over-engineering this project guards against.
